decisions.evidence: r3 maker: 'a single box — just the link, one click, to keep saving fast'; r3 client: 'one link and one click is exactly the speed I want'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Save-by-url presented and conforms to reference; recorded conforming decision.

decisions.evidence: r3 maker: 'I generated a readable one from the link... I assumed a title helps'; entry shows only title+link+timestamp. r3 client: 'use the page's real title and, when available, show its description, site icon, and preview image—not make a title from the address.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Presented title-from-URL and entry omitting description/favicon/preview contradicts REF-BM-02 (auto-collect real metadata) and REF-BM-07 (expose title/description/favicon). Client supplies reference-conforming behaviour.

decisions.evidence: r3 maker save flow has no edit step; r3 client: 'I should be able to correct the title and description both while saving and afterward.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Editing auto-collected title/description before and after save was missing from presented scope; client requests the reference requirement (extend).

decisions.evidence: r3 maker: link 'should drop straight into your list below as a new entry'; r3 client: 'if I paste a link I've already saved, please take me to the existing entry so I can edit it instead of adding another copy.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Presented save always adds a new entry, omitting duplicate-converges-to-edit (REF-BM-06); client requests it (extend). Delivered conforming in r5-r6.

decisions.evidence: r4 maker: 'clicking the title opens the original page in a new tab'; r4 client: 'having the title open the original page feels natural.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Item click navigating to original url conforms; the title-vs-link opener is an equivalent UI choice.

decisions.evidence: r5 maker edit only: 'Change the title or description'; r5 client: 'the edit action should let me correct the bookmark's address too... Once tags and notes are part of an entry, I'd expect to edit those there as well.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Presented edit omitted url/tags/note fields required by REF-BM-04; client requests the missing edit scope (extend). Address field added r6.

decisions.evidence: r7 maker describes search net without stating case behaviour; r7 client: 'Search should ignore capitalisation.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Case-insensitive search (REF-BM-13) was absent from the presented search description; client requests it (extend by omission).

decisions.evidence: r7 maker: search matches 'title, description, and address'; r7 client: 'any notes I add to a bookmark should also be searchable.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Presented full-text scope omitted the note field required by REF-BM-12; client extends search to notes.

decisions.evidence: r7 maker search covers only free words over title/description/address; r7 client: '#tag to search by tag'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. #tag search (REF-BM-14) missing from presented scope; client requests it (extend).

decisions.evidence: r7 maker presents plain live filtering only; r7 client: 'quotation marks for an exact phrase, and AND, OR, NOT, and parentheses... should only act as search instructions when unquoted; if I put one in quotation marks, it should be searched as an ordinary word.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Advanced query syntax — exact phrase (REF-BM-16) and boolean/parentheses with quoted-operator-literal rule (REF-BM-15) — absent from presented scope; client requests it (extend).

decisions.evidence: r8 maker: 'Only uppercase AND/OR/NOT act as instructions; lowercase and/or/not are treated as ordinary words.' r8 client: 'AND, OR, and NOT should work regardless of capitalisation... If I want one of those words treated as an ordinary search term, I'll put it in quotation marks.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Presented case-based operator distinction contradicts REF-BM-15's rule that operators are literal only when quoted; client supplies the reference-conforming rule (correct).

decisions.evidence: r9 maker: 'Two fixed groups only — To read and Reference — as a built-in split.' r9 client: 'I wouldn't make To read and Reference permanent, mutually exclusive types. I'd treat To read as a status... a quick Mark as read... It should disappear from the To read view but remain in my main collection.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Presented mutually-exclusive fixed types contradict the unread-flag status model (REF-BM-17 mark unread, REF-BM-18 unread view, REF-BM-19 mark read to remove); client supplies the conforming status model (correct).

decisions.evidence: r9 maker only floats 'more than two states (e.g. an archived/done as well)?'; r9 client: 'I do also want Archive, but as a separate state... hide a bookmark from the normal list and normal searches while keeping it available in its own Archived view, and I should be able to restore it. That should remain different from permanently deleting it.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Archive as a distinct reversible state (REF-BM-26), archived-only view (REF-BM-28) and archive-vs-delete distinction (REF-BM-27) were not in the presented model; client specifies them (extend).

decisions.evidence: r10 maker offered choice: 'I haven't added a delete action yet. Do you want an outright Delete (with a confirm) available too, or is Archive enough for now?' r10 client: 'Please add permanent Delete as well, with a confirmation that clearly distinguishes it from Archive... cancelling the confirmation must leave it untouched.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Offered alternatives differ in fulfilment of REF-BM-05 (the 'Archive is enough' option omits delete); client selects the reference-conforming alternative with the permanent-vs-reversible distinction (REF-BM-27).

decisions.evidence: r12 maker: tags as chips, 'Click a tag chip... filters your collection to everything carrying that tag'; r12 client: 'clicking a tag to filter the collection is exactly what I want.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Assign tags (REF-BM-09) and tag-filter (REF-BM-11) presented and conform.

decisions.evidence: r12 maker: tag entry by Enter/comma chips, no suggestions; r12 client: 'I do want suggestions from my existing tags as I type, so I can select one instead of accidentally creating a near-duplicate.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Tag autocomplete from existing tags (REF-BM-10) missing from presented tag entry; client requests it (extend). Delivered r13.

decisions.evidence: r14 maker presents notes as plain 'text in a highlighted panel'; r14 client: 'I do want notes to support Markdown formatting. I should edit the Markdown text, then see the formatted result—such as headings, lists, links, and emphasis—when viewing.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Presented plain-text note omits markdown rendering required by REF-BM-23; client requests markdown edit-and-render (extend). Delivered r15.

decisions.evidence: r17 maker 'What's settled (12 flows)' scope summary omits bulk actions; r17 client: 'Select several bookmarks and add or remove tags, mark them read or unread, archive them, or delete them together. I also want the option to apply an action to every bookmark in the current search or view—not the entire collection accidentally.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Multi-select bulk actions (REF-BM-20) and apply-to-current-filter with scope safety (REF-BM-21) were absent from the maker's declared complete scope; client demands their inclusion before approval (extend).

decisions.evidence: r17 scope summary omits sorting; r17 client: 'Sort bookmarks by date added, title, and similar useful choices.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Sort by sort key (REF-BM-22) missing from settled scope; client requests it (extend). Delivered r18-r19.

decisions.evidence: r17 scope summary omits offline/archive capture; r17 client: 'Save an offline copy... A normal page should be kept as a single local page file; a PDF link should preserve the PDF instead. I'd also like the option to submit a page to the Internet Archive.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Local HTML/PDF snapshot with the PDF rule (REF-BM-24) and Internet Archive submission (REF-BM-25) absent from settled scope; client requests both (extend). Delivered r23.

decisions.evidence: r17 scope summary omits bundles; r17 client: 'Save a frequently used combination of search text plus included and excluded tags, so I can reopen that filtered collection later.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Saved bundle of search term + included/excluded tags (REF-BM-29) missing from settled scope; client requests it (extend). Delivered r22.

decisions.evidence: r17 scope summary omits import/export; r17 client: 'Import and export a standard browser-bookmarks HTML file, retaining titles, tags, and original saved dates where available.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Netscape HTML import (REF-BM-30) and export (REF-BM-31) absent from settled scope; client requests both with field preservation (extend). Delivered r24.

decisions.evidence: r17 scope summary omits settings; r17 client: 'Personal display choices such as the default sort, how many items are shown, and text size.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Display personal settings (REF-BM-32) missing from settled scope; client requests it (extend). Delivered r25-r26.

decisions.evidence: r20 maker: applying an action targets ticked bookmarks 'which can include ones scrolled off or filtered out after you ticked them'; r20 client: 'changing the search or switching views should clear the selection so I can't accidentally act on bookmarks that have become hidden.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Presented rule lets ticked items persist and be acted on outside the current filter, contradicting REF-BM-21's edge rule that bulk scope is limited to the current filter; client corrects to clear selection on filter/view change (correct). Distinct decision from the r17 omission-extend of the same item.
